payout_quote: Under Section 25C rules applicable through December 31, 2025: up to $1,200 combined annual cap for insulation, windows, doors, and energy audits. For 2026 work: live utility insulation rebates as listed per-utility on DSIRE (e.g., ~$600 insulation bonuses offered by major utilities in 2026).
timing: Utility rebates are typically paid 4-8 weeks after the insulation work is completed and documented. The federal 25C credit is closed for property placed in service after December 31, 2025.
eligibility: Set by each utility program: generally must be a residential customer of the utility; measures must meet the program's specs (R-value, air-sealing); many programs require a home energy audit or pre-approval before work begins.
catches: The federal insulation tax credit (25C, up to $1,200/year) EXPIRED December 31, 2025 — not available for 2026 work.
Remaining rebates are utility-specific and typically a few hundred dollars, not $1,000.
You must pay for the insulation work first — this is a discount on spending, not money earned.
Many programs require pre-approval or an energy audit BEFORE the work; doing the work first can disqualify you.
steps: Find insulation and air-sealing rebates for your zip code at https://dsireusa.org and on your utility's website.
Check whether the program requires pre-approval or a home energy audit before work — complete that step first if so.
Have the qualifying insulation/air-sealing work done by a qualified contractor and keep all invoices.
Submit the utility's rebate form with proof of purchase/installation; the rebate arrives as a bill credit or check, typically in 4-8 weeks.
biggest_catch: The federal insulation tax credit expired December 31, 2025 — remaining rebates are utility-specific, typically a few hundred dollars, and require paying for the insulation work first; it is a discount, not income.
notes: CORRECTION vs the route: the $1,000 top end was reachable under the old federal 25C credit; 2026 reality is utility rebates in the low hundreds. energy.gov/savings failed to load this session, so the live-utility channel is verified via DSIRE instead.
